report.source_text: in addition to the left sided infarct, we noticed that the left cerebral hemisphere was universally atrophic with ventricular enlargement. There was also evidence of calvarial thickening on the ipsilateral side, and hyperpneumatization of the left frontal sinus (Fig. 1).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 13-year-old girl initially presented with headaches starting at age 7, right hemiparesis with power 4/5, reduced sensation, brisk reflexes, minimal facial asymmetry, and was later noted to have complex-partial seizures one year after initial presentation. Initial head CT revealed a left parieto-temporal infarct with cerebral atrophy. A thorough thrombophilia workup was negative. Follow-up imaging a year later demonstrated universal atrophy of the left cerebral hemisphere with ventricular enlargement, calvarial thickening, and hyperpneumatization of the ipsilateral left frontal sinus, classic features supporting Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome.
